name: held-out example
wording: An example the architect holds back from the builders when a story's risk warrants, given only to its reviewers, so passing the visible examples while missing the concept is caught. It is held back by omission alone, never named to a builder or mentioned, since a prohibition would announce it. When one fails, builders learn the concept and the shortfall but not the case, and a case revealed to fix it becomes visible and is replaced by a new held-out one.
reason: The operator, 2026-10-15: the workflow becomes intent-based delegation instead of a prescribed procedure; each role is defined by what it receives and hands over, each handover states what it must contain, and established practice is named rather than restated. Held-out examples are a specialist means for a story's risk and are used in review.
